newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends sharply off, ample supply blamed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends sharply off, ample supply blamed.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended Monday with sharp losses for the third consecutive session on forecasts of higher temperatures in the "heating oil belt" of the northeastern United States amid ample supply.
"We have weather services calling for several days of warming when refiners are now pretty well positioned with supplies," said Jeff Foose, dealer with KCS Energy Inc in New Jersey.
February heating oil settled off 1.50 cents a gallon at 66.94 cents, down almost three cents since last Monday. Feb crude ended 18 cents lower at $25.23 a barrel.
Feb gasoline finished off 0.86 cent a gallon at 67.23 cents.

Technically the 14-day Relative Strength Indicator for Feb heat was entering an oversold condition of 39, but Jake Bernstein, chartist and president of MBH Commodity Advisors in Illinois, said heat will continue weak.

"We are done with heating oil, and we are now entering a good downtrend," said Bernstein, citing 65.30 as support for Feb heat using a computer-based formula. Other dealers pegged an area of support around 65.00 cents, citing a series of session lows in early November on a spot continuation chart.
Temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world, will rise to above average this week and then turn below normal Friday through Monday, meteorologists said.
But, they said the upcoming cold snap will not be as cold as last week's.

"The arctic airmass does not look nearly as strong as the one during the past week, but it will send temperatures below normal levels across the eastern half of the nation for a three-to-four day period," said Jon Davis, meteorologist with Smith Barney in Chicago.

Supplies of distillate, particularly heating oil, were deemed more than sufficient in the New York Harbor, leaving no takers earlier Monday for several New York Harbor-bound distillate cargoes, including shipments by British Petroleum and Vitol SA, cash traders said.
And, even more heating oil was on its way to New York.

Colonial Pipeline Co said last week that it would continue rationing space on a distillate line through February because it was still faced with more shipment requests than the 960,000 barrel per day line could handle.
The line under rationing runs from Houston to Greensboro, North Carolina where it branches off to the New York Harbor.

Dealers said Feb crude lost ground Monday since funds began rolling positions from the February contract into March ahead of the Feb contract's expiry on Tuesday. Feb gasoline fell in sympathy with heating oil and crude.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
